scope: Compare installed GTK2 scrollbar stepper painting at adjustment limits with the normal and whole-widget-insensitive states, without changing the theme or user session.

method.fixture: Native GtkHScrollbar and GtkVScrollbar loaded with the user's installed DomainOS GTK2 RC in a private Xvfb; no application window, desktop, or MAME instance was touched.
method.normal: Capture at an interior adjustment value; crop each 15x15 stepper cell.
method.range_endpoint: Press and release each direction at its blocked lower/upper boundary; verify adjustment remains unchanged; crop the corresponding 15x15 cell.
method.whole_widget_insensitive: Capture the same two GTK2 scrollbar widgets after setting the entire widgets insensitive.
method.comparison: Exact RGBA pixel comparison against the current generated KDE-role normal and disabled cell assets.

observed.result: At range boundaries GTK2 paints the stepper cell with the disabled-role appearance while keeping the scrollbar interactive overall and correctly blocking movement in the unavailable direction. The whole-widget-insensitive fixture produces the same cell appearance. This conflicts with the shared scrollbar contract, which requires a range-boundary arrow to preserve the enclosing scrollbar palette while retaining the blocked input state.

source_analysis.finding: draw_stepper chooses GTK_STATE_INSENSITIVE for either a parent GtkRange that is insensitive or a stepper whose lower/upper range is unavailable. It then passes that state, the widget, and the stepper detail to gtk_paint_box. The GtkStyle draw_box interface receives widget/detail, and public GtkRange APIs expose the adjustment, inversion and lower/upper sensitivity policy. This gives a concrete custom-renderer experiment: determine whether a boundary-disabled stepper can be distinguished from a whole insensitive widget while preserving input blocking. Direction/inversion handling and renderer integration are not yet prototyped or proven. A pixmap RC state mapping alone cannot distinguish the two causes.

limits: The generated GTK2 preview establishes current runtime behavior, not the appearance of XtSensitive=False in the Domain/OS SR10.4 VM.
No VM capture or input was used; no VUE disabled-state evidence is claimed.
The result does not identify the application and state behind the user's original report; Q501 remains unanswered.
A GTK RC state-to-image remap alone cannot be assumed safe because the boundary and whole-widget-insensitive fixtures currently produce the same GTK state appearance.
V03 remains partial and unreviewed; no user acceptance is inferred.
status: GTK2 range-endpoint state mismatch confirmed in isolated native preview; implementation investigation remains open
